summary:
Ground truth is origin/main 15e78e276 (read-only worktree ground-main-20260924; vitest NOT RUN because apps/reading/node_modules is absent there). Antiek has a subagent "thread" only in the loose sense of an investigation id with a per-investigation JSONL event log. You can see what a research did (process) at /replay/:id and what it concluded (outcome) at /inv/:id, which shows the MasterMdViewer answer, the DistillView insights and questions, and AutoNotebook. Both are persisted and reachable. The mothership mechanics the operator described are missing or disconnected:
(1) No document or project has a thread list. The Reader's "Saved chases" rail is keyed to localStorage handoffs whose parent is read-<doc>, and no shipped Reader action ever writes one. Highlight to Deep-research in the Reader calls spin-research, which parents the research to a global "read-spin" pseudo-thread and navigates away. The backend researches_for_passage() has no route.
(2) You cannot ask a prior research thread a follow-up that carries its context. "Chat · this investigation" and Follow-this launch a new child whose only context is the question or highlight text. Loop One never reads the parent's synthesis or notes. The project-note injection module (note_injection) has no production caller. The prior-knowledge reuse step emits a knowledge.reused event, but the assembled pack is thrown away, both in Loop One and in HostLocalRunner.
(3) The only context carry that works is client-side: TalkToBook sends the active branch's history, but it lives in sessionStorage, and Wrestle keeps working memory inside one session-scoped investigation.
(4) Merge exists only as a view-layer concatenation. "Draft merge" in ArtifactOutlineShelf writes a static HTML file with file:// links; there is no queryable merged context. Automatic merge is absent.
(5) Companion documents exist per investigation (AutoNotebook, MasterMdViewer, twin-notes.html, artifact.html). Nothing accumulates across a project's threads. The per-document companion rail shows only marginalia and voice-note notes, not findings from researches spun off that document. The per-asset twin store (/twins) is mounted but has no producer and no UI.
(6) Merge-into-document is partial: blocks can be dragged into a Write outline with graph provenance, and a deliverable can be seeded from an investigation. The only "merge into a document" backend (source-merge commit) appends the draft-merge HTML into documents.raw_text in place. That contradicts the accepted Safe Derived Asset Merge (SDAM) decision ("never mutates a book") and is effectively unreachable today.
(7) Forks with lineage exist only as a schema. SDAM's derived_assets and derived_asset_revisions tables (with parent_revision_id) have zero writers. Doc version history is spec-only: notebook edits are destructive UPDATE and DELETE. The Write Cmd+K edit applies with no diff or accept step. The cross-workflow ThreadBreadcrumb and ThreadJump plus GET /thread/{node_id} are built but never mounted.

risks: The source-merge commit rewrites a SOURCE book in place: it appends the entire draft-merge HTML document into documents.raw_text between comment markers (source_merge.py:214-226,400-414). The accepted SDAM decision says merge must never mutate a book (safe-derived-asset-merge-boundary.md:11-16), and derived_asset_boundary.py treats these fields as a rejected legacy contract, yet /research/artifacts/source-merge/commit stays mounted (artifact_routes.py:474) and the ReadingCompanion 'rewrite source' button calls it. It is unreachable today only because no Reader action records a handoff. A fix to C01 that populates handoffs would arm it. The request is also authorized by a client-supplied operator_reviewer string ('reader-companion', ReadingCompanion.tsx:190,255), and I saw no document-owner check in the route.

Vacuous flywheel: knowledge.reused is emitted, but the reuse pack is dropped in both Loop One (orchestrator.py:1851-1865 with investigation_start_reuse.py:92-101) and HostLocalRunner (host_local.py:291-302). /health flywheel_ready (app.py:334-370) can report compounding that never reached a prompt. Evidence is READ only; no prompt capture was RUN.

Thread state is fragmented across six stores: sessionStorage (talk branches, thought partner, the Wrestle investigation id), localStorage (chase handoffs, the investigation-tree map), per-investigation JSONL, DuckDB, and the filesystem (~/.antiek/research-artifacts; ~/.antiek/twins JSON outside the single writer and possibly outside backups). Any thread index must reconcile them or it will contradict itself.

The twin routes (/twins, /twins/merge) and the compose routes take no Request/owner and do no ownership checks (twin_notes_routes.py:60-120; artifact_routes.py:325-380). That is fine single-operator, but it becomes a cross-owner read/merge hole when multi-user arrives.

Book-spawned research lineage lives in one ever-growing global 'read-spin' trajectory (passage_research.py:135-199), and GET /investigations scans the whole events directory per call (app.py:3001-3060). Per-document or per-project thread lists built on scans will degrade. They need an indexed table written through the single writer.

The name 'thread' is overloaded: SPR-06 cross-workflow entity thread (shell/threadModel.ts), readingThreadId read-<doc>, TalkThread branches, the ThoughtPartner thread, and feedback threads. A mothership spec must pick one canonical noun and rename the rest, or the UI and API will collide.
open_questions: Is a 'workstation/project' a new entity that owns several root researches, documents and drafts, or is it a root investigation, as it is today (ResearchWorkstation/index.tsx:61-86)? Per-project thread lists and companions depend on this.
useTalkThread.ts:14-22 cites an 'operator decision' to keep talk-to-book in session state, while antiek-reader SPR-06 plans durable anchored threads. Which decision stands?

What exactly is a completed research thread's 'held context' for a follow-up: synthesis only, synthesis plus distilled nodes, the trajectory summary, or the raw sources? What token budget, and which role answers (a cheap Q&A turn over the pack, or a new child research)?
Automatic merge policy: which threads auto-merge (same document? same project? parent/child?), is it view-level (the companion doc) or context-level (the agent pack), and is it reversible?
Should the Reader source-merge chain be retired now in favour of SDAM derived assets, as the decision record implies, or kept behind a flag until SDAM SPR-01/02 lands?
Is the /twins filesystem store the intended per-document companion substrate, or legacy to delete? It has no producer on main.

vitest was NOT RUN (apps/reading/node_modules absent in the ground worktree). Should a follow-up RUN ReadingCompanion, ArtifactOutlineShelf, ChaseThread and useTalkThread tests to back these READ claims behaviourally?
